- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 85+ values) — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too late.
- Underestimates when true values show strong downward momentum (e.g., 85→75 range) — model fails to recognize mean reversion.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the medium term (7–15 days).
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward trends — true drops often occur before model adjusts.
- When history includes a recent high, model often overcorrects downward, then fails to recover.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent volatility — model reacts to noise rather than structural trends.
- Model underestimates when true values are clustered near the bottom of the range (e.g., 75–76) — fails to recognize support levels.
- Model tends to smooth out sharp drops, underestimating the depth of the fall.
- Forecasts often overshoot the true mean by 2–5% in the first 3–5 days, then converge toward true mean.
